terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: Not solved and deliberately not matched to the reference. The review camera is fixed by the consumer harness (scripts/breadlab.ts applyView).

objectClass.primaryType: small cluster of three whole black olives
objectClass.notes: Matte faceted clay shading, flat color facets only -- prompt JSON explicitly excludes any shine ('never as shine'). Consumer runtime is a stylized low-poly showcase, so target look is faceted matte clay rather than food photorealism.

reasoning: Three near-identical macro bodies (olive-a/b/c) differing only in XZ offset, yaw and one extra tilt, so componentCount scores 1 rather than 3.
Silhouette is three smooth prolate ellipsoids with only a mild asymmetric taper, scoring silhouetteComplexity 1.
Repetition density scores 1: only 3 instances (lower than pancake's ~40-pit micro field), placed by hand rather than a scatter system.
One material family in two albedo zones (body vs upper-face cap), so materialLayerCount scores 1.

Local detail density scores 1: the pit-cavity opening visible in the reference is deliberately dropped (see spec risks) as sub-legibility at the 64px thumbnail target, leaving only the tilt orientation and taper asymmetry as authored cues.
Occlusion risk scores 1: the back olive's far side is hidden but fully inferable by radial symmetry.
Action readiness scores 0: static turntable showcase prop, no pivots/sockets/colliders beyond a bounding proxy.
Aggregate 7/24 with no axis above 1 confirms the simple tier.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Simple tier by part count, but still needs meso depth (each olive's cap patch is a separately shaded, separately masked sub-region) and one repetition system for the 3-instance cluster placement.

detailInventory.note: Enumerated by hand from the three supplied reference views rather than by build_detail_inventory.py (a 3x3 grid scan would emit nine crops of the same three simple bodies and add no detail the curated prompt spec does not already name) -- CRIB.md skip rule for single-repeated-system objects.

details.zone: upper mid-length patch of every olive
details.observation: A muted olive-green facet region (#5C6B3E) sits on the upper-facing surface of each olive, distinct from the dominant deep aubergine-black body (#3B2F2F), as a hard facet edge with no gradient.
details.inference: Stylized key-light-catching highlight rendered as flat color rather than shading.

details.observation: One olive (front-left in the reference) is rotated so its broader, more rounded (blunt) end points toward the camera rather than lying broadside like the other two.
details.inference: Compositional choice to demonstrate the asymmetric taper / pit-end silhouette.

details.observation: Each olive's two ends are not mirror-symmetric: one end (blunt) stays wide over more of the length, the other (stem) narrows sharply.
details.inference: Natural olive morphology -- stem attachment point tapers faster than the blossom end.
details.evidenceRef: olive-2.png front elevation, all three instances

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

mustMatch: three-olive cluster silhouette with all three individually readable
asymmetric taper: blunt end broader for longer, stem end narrows sharper
two-tone body/cap facet split, surviving the runtime Lambert swap
one olive tilted to show its blunt end
faceted flat shading baked into geometry
niceToHave: the reference's pit-cavity opening at one olive's blunt tip -- deliberately dropped, see spec risks

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: One olive tilted to show its blunt end
All three olives rest on the shared ground, no floating parts
Faceted flat shading baked into geometry

nextRequiredEvidence: Important visible forms are represented in component geometryDescriptor, deformations, localFeatures, or repetitionSystems.
Endpoint-based child parts are rooted at their attachment sockets and do not visibly float away from parents.
no floating child roots/joints in the browser screenshot
browser render screenshot from your agent's browser/screenshot tool
side-by-side reference/render comparison sheet for AI vision review
banded interior difference vs the reference baseline (forge/stage4_review/interior_difference.py --from/--to per region)
AI vision score at or above the visual acceptance threshold
all critical semantic feature scores from the shared image pair at or above their thresholds
self-correction review appended with action=continue before the next pass

droppedPasses.lighting-pass: lighting is fixed by the consumer harness and is not authorable in the model (spec.lookDevTargets.lightingPass.authority)
droppedPasses.interaction-pass: static showcase prop with no sockets, hinges or colliders beyond a bounding proxy; preSpecAssessment scores actionReadinessNeed 0

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: See qualityContract.featureGroups.reference-lookdev.documentedLimitation: the consumer runtime keeps only map and color, and the repo bans PBR maps outright, so every channel these fields describe is inert. All of it is moved into geometry.

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold

lightingPass.authority: Lighting is fixed by the consumer, not authored here: scripts/breadlab.ts mirrors scripts/thumbsHarness.ts with a warm directional key 0xffe2b0 at (-2, 6, 2) intensity 1.4, an ambient 0xfff0dc at 0.75 and a cool fill 0xdce8ff at (2.5, 3, -2) intensity 0.2.
mustAvoid: relying on a contact shadow the harness does not render

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: The far side of the back olive (olive-c) is never directly visible at any reviewed azimuth above the horizon; resolved by construction (full radial symmetry per shell before jitter).
The runtime normalizes the cluster's longest axis to 1.6, so absolute dimensions are arbitrary and only the authored ratios/offsets carry meaning.
The green cap patch position is not identity-critical at pixel precision; its presence, tonal contrast, and mid-length placement are what the review scores.

coordinateFrame.front: +Z, the direction the harness three-quarter camera at (-1.6, 2.2, 2.6) looks from
coordinateFrame.scaleReference: OLIVE_RADIUS = 0.44 relative unit at each olive's own equator. Absolute scale is meaningless: the consumer runtime refits the cluster's longest axis to 1.6, so only ratios and relative offsets matter (types.ts section 7).

silhouette.boundingShape: compact triangular cluster of three prolate ellipsoids, roughly 2.0 wide by 1.15 tall by 1.7 deep in relative units

aspectRatios.source: olive-2.png: widest point sits slightly toward the blunt end, not at heightFraction 0

silhouette.symmetry: each olive is approximately radially symmetric about its own long axis (broken slightly by surface jitter); the cluster as a whole is asymmetric
dominantCurves: smooth convex taper from equator to each pole, asymmetric rate
negativeSpaces: shallow contact creases where olives touch -- the only negative space in the group silhouette
landmarks: widest point near heightFraction -0.08 of each olive
green cap patch confined to a mid-length upper band, never reaching either pole
front-left olive's blunt pole tilted toward the camera

observations: three plump prolate-ellipsoid olives resting together, touching but not overlapping the group silhouette
front-left olive is tilted so its blunt end (rounder, broader taper) points toward the camera
each olive carries a muted olive-green facet patch on its upper-facing surface, never a full ring
each olive's length:width ratio is roughly 1.55:1
widest point sits slightly toward the blunt end, not at the exact midpoint
blunt end tapers more gradually than the stem end (broader for longer)
three olives form a compact triangular footprint, all mutually touching
no olive fully hides another's footprint from directly above

componentTree.name: Olive Cluster
componentTree.topologyRationale: Transform-only assembly node carrying the three olive bodies; it emits no geometry of its own. Its primitive mirrors its children's so no other primitive family is implied.

collider.notes: Ellipsoid bounding proxy; sufficient for a static showcase prop.

colorMaterialRecipe.materialClassRationale: Closest class in the allowed set for a matte faceted ingredient prop: opaque dielectric, roughness 1.0, no specular lobe. The reference explicitly excludes glossy/oil-sheen response.

localFeatures.name: Three-olive resting cluster
localFeatures.description: Three olives placed with independent XZ offsets and yaw so each remains individually readable in the group silhouette (types.ts R1); all three share the ground plane at world Y=0 after each instance's own bounding-box floor correction.

surfaceDetail.normalPattern: faceted planar shading from split vertices
surfaceDetail.displacementPattern: none -- shape carried entirely by the revolved profile
surfaceDetail.occlusionPattern: none -- runtime Lambert has no AO channel; underside darkening comes from N.L falloff alone
surfaceDetail.edgeWearPattern: none -- a whole, unblemished olive carries no wear
surfaceDetail.notes: Assembly node; no surface of its own.

componentTree.name: Olive body (a)
componentTree.topologyRationale: One continuous, smoothly varying rotationally symmetric mass -- a prolate-ellipsoid shell revolved from a single monotonic profile, poles at each tip. Decision tree step 6. Not a sphere primitive because the reference shows a clear asymmetric taper (blunt end broader, stem end narrower), which only a custom profile carries.

deformationStack.notes: Uniform per-vertex position noise, amplitude 0.016 (0.036 of equatorial radius), applied while the shell is still indexed so the cap/body shared triangle boundary moves together and never tears (R1).

geometryDescriptor.uvStrategy: top-planar projection per material bucket (scripts/breads/lib.ts uvTopPlanar) -- no texture is emitted, UVs exist only for merge attribute consistency
geometryDescriptor.normalStrategy: flat normals baked by splitting vertices after jitter, never a flatShading flag

collider.notes: Ellipsoid bounding proxy; sufficient for a static showcase prop.

colorMaterialRecipe.materialClassRationale: Closest class in the allowed set for a matte faceted ingredient prop: opaque dielectric, roughness 1.0, no specular lobe. The reference explicitly excludes glossy/oil-sheen response.

seams.notes: Boundary between olive-body and olive-cap is a triangle-index split on one shared indexed shell (splitTrianglesByVertexMask), not a separate geometry -- watertight by construction, no seam-overlap risk.

localFeatures.name: Asymmetric pole taper
localFeatures.description: Blunt pole (heightFraction -1) tapers gradually (radius stays above 0.55 until heightFraction -0.80); stem pole (+1) tapers sharply (radius drops below 0.22 by heightFraction 0.80).

localFeatures.name: Tilted to show blunt end
localFeatures.description: This instance carries an extra rotation.z (tiltZ) beyond the shared lay-down rotation, lifting its blunt pole toward the three-quarter camera so the broader taper reads clearly, per geometry.silhouette in assets/prompts/ingredients/olive.json.

surfaceDetail.displacementPattern: none -- shape carried entirely by the revolved profile
surfaceDetail.occlusionPattern: none -- runtime Lambert has no AO channel; underside darkening comes from N.L falloff alone
surfaceDetail.edgeWearPattern: none -- a whole, unblemished olive carries no wear
surfaceDetail.notes: Body tone covers the lower/shaded majority of the shell. The runtime replaces the material with MeshLambertMaterial keeping only map and color, so all shape relief here is geometric.

componentTree.name: Olive upper-face color cap (a)
componentTree.topologyRationale: Not a separate solid -- a subset of the parent olive-body's own triangles, selected by a per-vertex mask (local Y above threshold, local X inside a mid-length band) after the shared shell is built and jittered, then split by triangle index. Recorded as its own component because it carries a distinct material and a distinct evidence-backed region, mirroring how pancake.ts models disk-*-face as a child of disk-*.

deformationStack.notes: Zero-displacement classification mask, not a geometry change: a vertex belongs to the cap bucket when local Y (post lay-down rotation) > 0.1 * OLIVE_RADIUS AND local X in [-0.5, 0.42] * OLIVE_HALF_LENGTH. A triangle is assigned to the cap bucket if any of its three vertices matches (lib.splitTrianglesByVertexMask), giving a mid-length upper patch that never reaches either pole -- matching olive.png where the green cast stops short of both tips.

geometryDescriptor.uvStrategy: top-planar projection per material bucket (scripts/breads/lib.ts uvTopPlanar)
geometryDescriptor.normalStrategy: flat normals inherited from the parent shell's split-vertex facet bake

seams.notes: Shares the parent shell's own triangles at the mask boundary; watertight because both buckets come from one indexed geometry split after jitter, never two independently built solids.

materials.name: Olive body (deep aubergine-black)
materials.shaderModel: MeshStandardMaterial carrier; the consumer runtime swaps it for MeshLambertMaterial keeping only map and color

albedo.samplingNotes: Hand-transcribed from assets/prompts/ingredients/olive.json geometry.surface, the curated prompt that generated these reference images. Deliberately NOT sampled from reference pixels, which carry the generator's baked key light.

textureProjection.texelDensityIntent: No texture is emitted. UVs exist only to satisfy the merge step's attribute-consistency requirement (scripts/ingredients/types.ts inherited section 4).

roughness.localResponse: inert -- the runtime Lambert swap discards roughness entirely

ambientOcclusion.notes: No AO channel: the runtime Lambert material has none.

localOverrides.name: Underside key-light falloff
localOverrides.description: No AO/dirt map is authored; the shaded lower-half hue (#4A3A36, prompts/ingredients/olive.json) is deliberately NOT painted as a second material -- the runtime key light already darkens the convex shell's underside via N.L falloff, so this is the equivalent effect achieved through geometry+lighting rather than a texture mask (see spec risk shaded-underside-hue-dropped).

shaderNotes: Emit via scripts/breads/lib.ts stdMaterial(): MeshStandardMaterial with roughness 1, metalness 0.
Never set vertexColors: the runtime rebuilds every material as MeshLambertMaterial({map, color}), so vertex colors are silently discarded.
Never set flatShading: that flag is not inherited by the runtime swap either. Faceting must be baked as split vertices.
materials.notes: lower/shaded majority of every olive. Two solid colors are enough for the whole cluster, so no texture is emitted at all (types.ts inherited section 9).

materials.name: Olive upper-face cast (muted olive-green)
materials.shaderModel: MeshStandardMaterial carrier; the consumer runtime swaps it for MeshLambertMaterial keeping only map and color

albedo.samplingNotes: Hand-transcribed from assets/prompts/ingredients/olive.json geometry.surface, the curated prompt that generated these reference images. Deliberately NOT sampled from reference pixels, which carry the generator's baked key light.

textureProjection.texelDensityIntent: No texture is emitted. UVs exist only to satisfy the merge step's attribute-consistency requirement (scripts/ingredients/types.ts inherited section 4).

roughness.localResponse: inert -- the runtime Lambert swap discards roughness entirely

displacement.pattern: mid-length upper patch of every olive

ambientOcclusion.notes: No AO channel: the runtime Lambert material has none.

localOverrides.name: Body/cap facet boundary
localOverrides.description: The boundary is a per-vertex position mask (local Y + local X band) applied to the shared indexed shell before triangle-index splitting -- a hard geometric edge between two meshes, not a texture boundary and not a vertex-color ramp.

shaderNotes: Emit via scripts/breads/lib.ts stdMaterial(): MeshStandardMaterial with roughness 1, metalness 0.
Never set vertexColors: the runtime rebuilds every material as MeshLambertMaterial({map, color}), so vertex colors are silently discarded.
Never set flatShading: that flag is not inherited by the runtime swap either. Faceting must be baked as split vertices.
materials.notes: mid-length upper patch of every olive. Two solid colors are enough for the whole cluster, so no texture is emitted at all (types.ts inherited section 9).

repetitionSystems.name: Three-olive resting cluster
repetitionSystems.elementKind: repeated macro body, each with its own body+cap child pair

distribution.mode: hand-placed XZ offsets with independent yaw and one tilted instance
distribution.note: Offsets read off olive-3.png (top-down footprint); yaw differs per instance so no two olives share a facing direction.

repetitionSystems.seedRule: Offsets/yaw are fixed authored values (read off the reference), not random; only the surface-jitter deformation consumes the builder rng, so the exported GLB is byte-deterministic.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Hard consumer budget for the 'cluster' ingredient group: <=700 tri and <=68KB target (types.ts R2), hard ceiling <=2500 tri and <=100KB (scripts/check-budget.mjs). Target reached by construction (12 segments x 8 profile rings x 3 olives = 432 tri before any mask split, mask split adds zero triangles), not by decimation.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Warm directional key 0xffe2b0 at (-2, 6, 2), intensity 1.4, upper-left -- the same relationship as the reference's 'single soft key light upper-left'.
lightingFromPhoto.usage: Fixed by scripts/breadlab.ts, mirrored from scripts/thumbsHarness.ts. Not authored by the model.
lightingFromPhoto.exposure: no exposure control and no tone mapping -- authored albedo lands on screen almost unchanged.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Ambient 0xfff0dc at 0.75 -- a high ambient ratio, which is why the underside darkening relies on the shell's own curvature turning away from the key light rather than a painted shadow tone.
lightingFromPhoto.contactShadow: none -- no shadow map, no ground plane rendered. The reference's contact shadow between touching olives is a known, accepted delta.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Cool directional fill 0xdce8ff at (2.5, 3, -2), intensity 0.2, opposite the key.
lightingFromPhoto.toneMapping: NoToneMapping (three.js default); no AO available on the runtime Lambert material.

proceduralStrategy: Revolve each olive's shell from the shared asymmetric-taper profile at the shared segment count.
Jitter vertices while the shell is still indexed, so the cap/body split never tears.
Classify triangles into the cap bucket by a local-space vertex mask (Y above threshold, X inside a mid-length band), never by vertex color.
Bake faceting by splitting vertices and recomputing normals; never request flatShading.
Project top-planar UVs per bucket, then merge all three olives by material into exactly two meshes.

Lay each shell on its side (fixed 90deg Z rotation baked before per-instance placement), add per-instance yaw and (for olive-a only) an extra tiltZ, then translate each instance's own bounding box floor to world Y=0.
animationAnchors: root pivot supports whole-cluster rotation for the showcase turntable
each olive is a named instance, so a future 'add an olive' animation can translate one instance without rebuilding the shared shell logic
destructionAnchors: each olive is its own fractureGroup; the only plausible break is one olive rolling away from the cluster, not a shattered olive

risks.description: assets/prompts/ingredients/olive.json names a third hue (#4A3A36) for the shaded lower half, which this spec does not wire to a material bucket.
risks.mitigation: mesh<=2 budget forces a 2-bucket split (types.ts section 1); the runtime key light already darkens the underside of a convex shell for free via N.L falloff, so painting a second dark tone into geometry would double-darken rather than add fidelity. Body bucket carries #3B2F2F everywhere except the cap patch.

risks.description: olive.png shows a small dark octagonal recessed opening at one olive's blunt tip (a pit-cavity look). This spec does not model it as geometry.
risks.mitigation: At the 300-700 tri cluster budget and the ~64px final thumbnail read distance, a sub-tip cavity is below the silhouette-legibility threshold; the orientation cue (tilt toward camera) is kept as the identity signal instead. Recorded here rather than silently dropped.

risks.description: Any vertex-color-based region paint is silently discarded by the runtime's MeshLambertMaterial swap, collapsing the two-tone split to one flat tone.
risks.mitigation: The body/cap split is carried by two separate materials on two separate triangle buckets from one shared indexed shell, split geometrically. No vertexPaint block is authored anywhere in this spec.

risks.description: A flatShading flag is not inherited by the runtime material swap, so a model relying on it renders smooth.
risks.mitigation: Faceting is baked into geometry by splitting vertices (scripts/breads/lib.ts facet) before export.

risks.description: Body and cap triangles come from the same shell; jittering after the mask split (rather than before) would let the shared boundary vertices move independently and open a crack.
risks.mitigation: Jitter runs once, on the whole indexed shell, before the mask/split step -- both buckets read the same already-jittered positions.

risks.description: mergeByMaterial throws when geometries in one bucket carry different attribute sets.
risks.mitigation: Every geometry gets exactly position, normal and uv; no color attribute is ever created; all six per-olive part geometries (3 olives x {body,cap}) route through the same uvTopPlanar call.
